trial_court: Metropolitan Magistrate (Mahila Court),South East, Saket, CRL.M.C. 894/2019
case_name: Kishan Kumar vs The State & Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: The State & Anr, Respondents (State and respondent no.2)

facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent no.2 got married, had two sons, but due to matrimonial differences started living separately. Respondent no.2 filed a written complaint which led to registration of FIR under sections 498A/506 IPC. Petitioner filed petitions for quashing of FIR and for settlement of disputes.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the respondent to establish that the settlement is not genuine.
legal_principles.held: The petitioner and the respondent no.2 stated that they have settled their disputes amicably without any fear, force and coercion.
cited_cases: Ganesh v. Sudhir Kumar Shrivastava and Ors., (2020) 20 SCC 787

legal_principles.principle: A settlement between the parties can dissolve their marriage as per Section 13(B) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
legal_principles.held: The petitioner and the respondent no.2 have agreed to dissolve their marriage as per section 13(B) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

outcome.final_order: FIR bearing no.529/2015 registered under sections 498A/506 IPC is quashed.

use_for_drafting: quashing FIRs in domestic violence cases
